title: Chiang Mai Tops the Yield Table at 14.2%
description: Five Chiang Mai condos measured against a 7.1% MRR benchmark — two buildings clear double-digit gross yields with entry prices under ฿1.3M.
lead: Chiang Mai is leading RealData's national yield ranking this week. Two buildings in Mueang and San Sai districts are printing gross yields above 14% on sub-฿1.3M average sale prices — a spread of more than 7 percentage points over the current Bank of Thailand MRR of 7.1%. That gap is wide enough to matter even after vacancy and management friction.

sections.heading: The High-Yield Pair: Entry Price vs. Return
sections.body:
[SR Complex](/condo/8402798c-1729-46cc-83a0-c757d206ab7f) leads at 14.2% gross yield on an average sale price of ฿1,267,180 and ฿15,000/month rent — the cheapest route to the top of this week's table. [The Private Condo](/condo/2a89868f-ee32-4a6a-bf25-96e454693e53) in San Sai is nearly identical: 14.01% yield, ฿1,208,413 average price, ฿14,106/month rent. The difference between the two is noise; execution risk — vacancy rate, lease terms, management quality — will determine which outperforms.

Both buildings are priced well below [The Spring Loft](/condo/63a6e160-6ff5-49a8-b742-7201f83209c9), which commands ฿3,097,000 average sale price but still delivers 10.53% gross yield on ฿27,185/month rent. That is a larger absolute rent, not a larger return — important if capital allocation rather than cash quantum is the objective.

sections.heading: Spread to MRR and What It Implies
sections.body:
At 7.1% MRR, the spread on SR Complex is +7.1 pp and on The Private Condo is +6.9 pp. [The Green City Condo](/condo/dd86d00c-2632-4292-ac23-939f84d6b948) at 8.81% and [SR Land Condominium](/condo/b956a205-6c11-4e2a-b739-733d6d256e03) at 7.98% still clear the benchmark, but the buffer shrinks fast once you model a single vacant month per year.

Chiang Mai's rental market is driven by a mix of digital nomads, university students, and retirees — demand that is real but seasonal. Buyers chasing the 14% headline should confirm whether the rent figures in our dataset reflect year-round occupancy or peak-season listings before committing capital.
